P.L. 119-4 (Full-Year Continuing Appropriations Act, 2025, division A) provides no Adoption Incentives rescission for FY2025. Deciding text, sec. 1101(a)(8) (139 Stat. 11; PDF p. 3; text layer): it continues 'The Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2024 (division D of Public Law 118-47), except section 240 shall be applied by substituting "$1,471,000,000" for "$1,250,000,000" ..., except sections 241 and 310, ...'. Section 241 of that division (P.L. 118-47, 138 Stat. 681) is the FY2024 rescission of $70,000,000 of P.L. 117-328 Children and Families Services Programs funds 'for grants to States for incentive payments, as defined by section 473A of the Social Security Act' -- the line the FY2024 tables print as 'Adoption Incentives (rescission)' -70,000. Sec. 1105 continues the referenced Acts' provisions only 'Except as otherwise expressly provided in this division'. The Labor-HHS title of the CR (title IX, secs. 1901-1912, 139 Stat. 31-33) adds no such rescission, and the whole law's text layer has no 'adoption', '473A' or 'incentive payments'. No committee table covers FY2025 Enacted (H.Rept. 119-271's 'FY 2025 Estimate' column is operating plans, held back).

P.L. 119-4 (Full-Year Continuing Appropriations Act, 2025, division A) provides no Adoption Incentives rescission for FY2025. Deciding text, sec. 1101(a)(8) (139 Stat. 11; PDF p. 3; text layer): it continues 'The Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2024 (division D of Public Law 118-47), except section 240 shall be applied by substituting "$1,471,000,000" for "$1,250,000,000" ..., except sections 241 and 310, ...'. Section 241 of that division (P.L. 118-47, 138 Stat. 681) is the FY2024 rescission of $70,000,000 of P.L. 117-328 Children and Families Services Programs funds 'for grants to States for incentive payments, as defined by section 473A of the Social Security Act' -- the line the FY2024 tables print as 'Adoption Incentives (rescission)' -70,000. Sec. 1105 continues the referenced Acts' provisions only 'Except as otherwise expressly provided in this division'. The Labor-HHS title of the CR (title IX, secs. 1901-1912, 139 Stat. 31-33) adds no such rescission, and the whole law's text layer has no 'adoption', '473A' or 'incentive payments'. No committee table covers FY2025 Enacted (H.Rept. 119-271's 'FY 2025 Estimate' column is operating plans, held back).
